title: Decomposing Brain-LLM Alignment with Interpretable Semantic Representations
abstract: arXiv:2610.21508v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) predict neural responses during naturalistic language comprehension, but the linguistic information underlying this brain alignment remains difficult to interpret. We use SCRIBE, an interpretable contextual semantic representation spanning 65 neurocognitively grounded semantic properties, as a lens for decomposing the brain alignment of one LLM, LLaMA2-7B. Using variance partitioning between LLaMA2-7B and SCRIBE on naturalistic fMRI data from seven participants listening to narrative stories (Moth Radio Hour), we separate brain-predictive variance shared between the two representations from variance unique to each. We find that shared variance is the dominant component across the whole brain and language-related regions, while both representations also retain significant unique contributions. translated_title: 基于可解释语义表示的大脑与大语言模型对齐分解
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）能够预测自然语言理解过程中的神经响应，但这种大脑对齐背后的语言学信息仍然难以解释。我们使用SCRIBE——一种涵盖65个基于神经认知的语义属性的可解释上下文语义表示——作为分析透镜，来分解大语言模型LLaMA2-7B的大脑对齐。通过对七名参与者在聆听叙事故事（Moth Radio Hour）时的自然场景fMRI数据进行LLaMA2-7B与SCRIBE之间的方差划分，我们将两种表示所共享的大脑预测方差与各自独有的方差分离开来。我们发现，共享方差是全脑及语言相关区域中的主导成分，同时两种表示也都保留了显著的独特贡献。我们进而考察各个语义属性的具体性程度是否与共享的及SCRIBE独有的大脑预测方差相关……
tldr: 该研究利用可解释语义表示SCRIBE与方差划分方法，将LLaMA2-7B的大脑对齐分解为与人类语义加工共享及各自独有的成分，发现共享方差在全脑及语言区域占主导地位，且语义属性的具体性与这些成分相关联。
en_tdlr: This study uses the interpretable semantic representation SCRIBE and variance partitioning to decompose LLaMA2-7B's brain alignment into shared and representation-unique components, finding that shared variance dominates across the whole brain and language regions, and that the concreteness of individual semantic properties relates to these components.
